questions.section: Section A: The participant, the plan and the practitioner
questions.text: Who is the participant, and which plan is this record for?
questions.hint: Write the name they go by and their NDIS number. Write the plan number from REG-SBS-01. That row holds the date we were engaged and the dates the plans are due.

controls.label: Then choose one: new plan; review

questions.section: Section A: The participant, the plan and the practitioner
questions.text: Who is the practitioner, what are their pathway and endorsed level, and is their learning current?
questions.hint: Write the date the Commissioner considered them suitable, their pathway (self-assessment or new entry-level) and their endorsed from FRM-SBS-01 Q6. Write the date of their last annual knowledge check (PRO-SBS-01 step 7) and of their last learning on restrictive practices and their risks. Read the dates from REG-HRM-02. If either is over 12 months old, stop and follow step 3 of PRO-SBS-02.

questions.section: Section A: The participant, the plan and the practitioner
questions.text: In which state or territory will the practice be used, and which note did you use?
questions.hint: Choose the state or territory. Write the date the note in REG-QMS-03 was last checked. Answer for each if the lives in, or moves between, two. If the note was last checked more than 6 months ago, has not been re-checked after an announced change, or is missing, stop and follow step 3 of PRO-SBS-02.

controls.label: Choose one or more states or territories

questions.section: Section B: The practice
questions.text: What is the practice, in plain words, and which kind is it?
questions.hint: Say what is done, where, when, by whom and for how long. Choose the kind with Decision table 1 in PRO-SBS-02. If it fits none of the five, say so and write the Clinical Supervisor's decision and reason.

questions.section: Section B: The practice
questions.text: If a medicine or a device is involved, is it used routinely or only as needed, and who confirmed what it is for?
questions.hint: Answer only when a medicine or a device is involved. Write its name, the name of the prescriber or health <button type="button" class="term" data-term="practitioner" data-def="in this policy, an NDIS behaviour support practitioner who works for us. The Commissioner considers the person suitable to do behaviour support assessments, including functional behavioural assessments. The Commissioner also considers them suitable to develop plans that may contain restrictive practices (the Rules, section 5)." data-source="POL-SBS-01">practitioner</button> and the date of their written answer on its purpose. Say that you sighted the current prescription or medication chart. Never write a dose, a time or a rate here. They stay in the prescriber's order, and the plan's protocol copies them from there exactly.

questions.section: Section B: The practice
questions.text: Is the practice in use now, and on what authority?
questions.hint: Ask each and read its use records. If you choose the third or fourth answer, write the date and time you told the provider in writing, and the PRO-SBS-05 record number.

options: in use under a current authorisation and in the plan

questions.section: Section B: The practice
questions.text: Does the state or territory prohibit this practice, or is it a high-risk practice the Commission says must never be in a plan?
questions.hint: Read the note's list of prohibited practices and the high-risk list in POL-SBS-02 C15 (prone or supine restraint, pin-downs and take-downs, restraint that restricts breathing or circulation, punitive or aversive practices, over-correction, seclusion of a child). If either answer is yes, the practice is never included, whatever is authorised. Write the date and time you told each implementing provider in writing.

controls.label: Date and time when either is yes

questions.section: Section C: People, authority and notice
questions.text: What does the participant need to take part, and how will we talk with them?
questions.hint: Read FRM-RGT-01 first. Write the format, interpreter, cultural support person, support person, place and time of day they chose.

questions.section: Section C: People, authority and notice
questions.text: Who did the participant agree you can involve?
questions.hint: Name each person and provider. Write the date each yes or no was recorded in FRM-INF-01. Write anyone they said no to, with their reasons: this is our record of all reasonable steps under section 20(3)(e) of the Behaviour Support Rules. Say whether an independent advocate was offered, accepted or refused.

controls.label: One line each: name; role; yes or no; date

questions.section: Section C: People, authority and notice
questions.text: Who has legal authority over a decision about this practice?
questions.hint: This may be a guardian, an administrator, a person with parental responsibility, a tribunal or an authorised officer. Write the document you sighted, what it covers, its date and its expiry. Write "the participant decides" where no one else has authority.

questions.section: Section C: People, authority and notice
questions.text: When and how was written notice of the intention to include the practice given?
questions.hint: Give notice to the participant, to each family member, carer or other person they chose, to any guardian or other person with legal authority, and to each provider that may use the practice. A person the participant refused at Q9 is not sent the notice. Write each person's name, the date and the format. For a comprehensive plan it must be at least 5 before the Clinical Supervisor decides; for an interim plan, at least 2 business days. Where the risk is immediate, write the reason.

controls.label: One line each: name; date; format

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: What risk of harm is the practice meant to answer?
questions.hint: Describe the behaviour, who could be harmed, how likely it is and how serious. Name the data you relied on and its dates.

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: Which risks of the practice did you explain, and to whom?
questions.hint: Cover injury, distress and trauma, loss of freedom, loss of skills and loss of trust. Add the risks that belong to this practice and this person. Write each person's name and the date.

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: How did each person show they understood the risks?
questions.hint: Ask each person to say the risks back in their own way, or to show you. Write what they said or did. Write "not yet understood" where that is true, and what you will try next.

controls.label: One line each: name; what they said or did; understood yes or not yet

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: Which alternatives were discussed or tried, and what happened?
questions.hint: List every less restrictive option, when it was tried, who suggested it and the result.

controls.label: One line each: alternative; dates tried; who suggested it; result

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: What does the participant think about the practice?
questions.hint: Write their view first, in their words or their way. Write any objection in full. Silence is not agreement.

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: What does each other person think about the practice?
questions.hint: Write each person's view and any objection. Include the person with legal authority and each implementing provider.

controls.label: One line each: name; view; objection yes or no

questions.section: Section D: Risks, alternatives and views
questions.text: Who was consulted, when and how?
questions.hint: Add a line for every meeting or call, including one that did not go ahead and why. Include the participant, each person at question 9, each implementing provider and each other specialist. Say which communication support was used.

controls.label: One line each: name; relationship or organisation; date; method; communication support

questions.section: Section E: Strategies and the case for the practice
questions.text: Who helped build the strategies, and what did each person contribute?
questions.hint: Include the participant, their network and each implementing provider. Write what each suggested and what each agreed to do.

controls.label: One line each: name; suggested; agreed to do

questions.section: Section E: Strategies and the case for the practice
questions.text: Which changes to the environment, skills and community activities will lessen the need for the practice?
questions.hint: List each one, who will do it and from when. Say which are applied now and which are not yet, and why.

controls.label: One line each: change, skill or activity; who; from when; applied yes or not yet

questions.section: Section E: Strategies and the case for the practice
questions.text: Why is the practice a last resort, and the least restrictive response possible?
questions.hint: Name the next less restrictive option and say why it does not yet keep people safe. Say which proactive strategies were applied first, and from when.

questions.section: Section E: Strategies and the case for the practice
questions.text: How does the practice reduce the risk of harm, and why is it in proportion to that risk?
questions.hint: Compare the harm at question 12 with the risks at question 13. Say why the harm is at least as serious as what the practice could cost.

questions.section: Section E: Strategies and the case for the practice
questions.text: What keeps each use to the shortest possible time?
questions.hint: Write the longest time one use may last, the sign that it must end and who ends it.

questions.section: Section F: Reduction and support
questions.text: What is the reduction and elimination strategy for this practice?
questions.hint: Write the goal, the steps in order and the measure. Write the point at which the practice is reduced and the point at which it ends. Answer for every practice, in an interim plan too.

questions.section: Section F: Reduction and support
questions.text: When will the practice next be reviewed?
questions.hint: For a comprehensive plan the date is no more than 12 months from the date of the plan. For an interim plan the date is the comprehensive plan's due date in REG-SBS-01 col I, never 12 months. List the changes that bring it forward: a change in behaviour, a new provider, an injury or a change in authorisation.

questions.section: Section F: Reduction and support
questions.text: What data will show progress, who collects it and how often?
questions.hint: Agree this with each implementing provider.

controls.label: One line each: data; collected by; how often; read by

questions.section: Section F: Reduction and support
questions.text: What support did we agree with each implementing provider?
questions.hint: Write the contact person, the training and coaching offered, the data they will send and the date of the first progress check. Ask the provider to confirm in writing.

controls.label: One line each: provider; contact; support; first check date; confirmed in writing yes or no

questions.section: Section G: The decision
questions.text: Did the practice and the draft plan pass each row of Decision table 2?
questions.hint: The Clinical Supervisor answers all 16 rows of Decision table 2 in PRO-SBS-02, row 16 (high-risk practice) first. Write the evidence for each.

controls.label: One answer for each of the 16 rows: yes

questions.trail: Asked at: ←PRO-SBS-01, step 13PRO-SBS-01 step 13

questions.section: Section G: The decision
questions.text: What did the Clinical Supervisor decide, and why?
questions.hint: Choose one and give reasons. If the participant objected, say how the objection was weighed.
questions.trail: Asked at: ←PRO-SBS-01, step 13PRO-SBS-01 step 13

questions.section: Section G: The decision
questions.text: How was each person told the decision?
questions.hint: Write each person's name, the date and the format. Tell each implementing provider in writing the same day if the practice is not included.

controls.label: One line each: name; date; format

questions.section: Section H: Lodgement and authorisation
questions.text: When was the plan lodged with the Commissioner?
questions.hint: Answer when the final plan holds a <button type="button" class="term" data-term="regulated restrictive practice" data-def="one of the five practices the Rules cover (section 6). Seclusion is sole confinement where the person cannot leave, such as a locked room. Chemical restraint is medicine given mainly to change behaviour. Mechanical restraint is a device that stops or limits movement, such as a strap or bed rails used for behaviour. Physical restraint is force used to stop or limit movement. Environmental restraint limits free access to parts of the person's environment, such as a locked cupboard or fridge." data-source="POL-SBS-01">regulated restrictive practice</button>. The Practitioner lodges in <button type="button" class="term" data-term="the Commission" data-def="the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. The Commissioner is its head." data-source="POL-SBS-01">the Commission</button>'s portal; the Service Manager may prepare the lodgement. Lodge every such plan, authorised or not, and every reviewed plan. If it was more than 5 business days after the plan was finalised, write the reason.

questions.section: Section H: Lodgement and authorisation
questions.text: Who applied for authorisation, and when was the request sent?
questions.hint: Answer when the note says an authorisation process exists. Write who applies: us, the implementing provider, a guardian or the participant. Write what was sent.

questions.section: Section H: Lodgement and authorisation
questions.text: What is the authorisation status of the practice?
questions.hint: Answer when the final plan holds a regulated restrictive practice. Add a new answer each time the status changes and keep the earlier ones. If declined, lapsed or withdrawn, write the date and time you told each implementing provider in writing that the practice must not be used.

questions.section: Section H: Lodgement and authorisation
questions.text: Which authorisation conditions and duties did you tell each implementing provider in writing?
questions.hint: Answer when the final plan holds a regulated restrictive practice. Tick each: use only as the plan sets, and only while authorised; the conditions and expiry; record each use and keep the record 7 years; report to the Commissioner each month, or every 2 weeks under a short-term approval; lodge evidence of authorisation; tell us of a change in circumstances; a use not authorised or not in the plan may be a reportable incident.

questions.section: Section I: Progress
questions.text: What did each progress check find?
questions.hint: Answer after the first progress check. Add a new dated entry for each check. Never overwrite an earlier entry.

controls.label: Dated entries: provider; data read; uses since the last check; progress against question 24

form.intro:
Use this record whenever a regulated restrictive practice is proposed for a participant's behaviour support plan, or is already in one. It shows who we talked with and which risks we explained. It shows which alternatives came first and why the practice is in proportion to the risk. It also shows how the practice will be reduced and ended.

This record authorises no restrictive practice. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory can do that.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this record. A provider that only carries out plans uses FRM-BSP-03 Restrictive Practice Authorisation and Consent Record.

  • One record covers one participant and one plan. Start a new record for each new plan, and for each review that adds, changes or removes a practice.
  • Answer questions 4 to 7, 12 to 17 and 19 to 35 once for each practice. The register keeps one row per practice per plan (the REG-SBS-01 practice sheet), so these answers are copied per practice.
  • The Behaviour Support Practitioner completes the record as each step of PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) is done. The record is in the order of the steps.
  • The Clinical Supervisor answers questions 28 and 29.
  • The practitioner adds a dated entry at question 35 after every progress check. Never overwrite an earlier entry.

Have ready:

  • The referral and the assessment so far.
  • The participant's communication preferences, in FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • The participant's consent record, in FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.
  • The incident and use records from each implementing provider.
  • The state or territory note, in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.
  • The practitioner's row in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register.

What happens next: the Service Manager copies each answer marked REG-SBS-01 to the row for this practice and this plan on the practice sheet of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register, in the column the question protocol pins. The record stays on the participant's file with the plan.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to decide whether a restrictive practice can be justified. We also use it to seek authorisation and to plan how to end the practice. The Behaviour Support Rules require us to consult the participant and the people around them. They also require us to lodge the plan with the NDIS Commission.

The practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the Service Manager read this record. We give parts of it to the authorising body of the state or territory and to the NDIS Commission. We share it with a provider that carries out the plan only as the law requires or the participant agrees. The same goes for the participant's support network. The law requires us to consult the providers who may use the practice and any person with legal authority, even if you ask us not to; we will tell you first and share only what they need.

If you are the participant, you can see this record and ask us to correct it. You can have an advocate with you. You can tell us you disagree, and we will write that down in your words.

POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Practitioner: send the record to the Clinical Supervisor with the draft plan, before the plan is finalised.
  • Clinical Supervisor: answer questions 28 and 29 within 5 business days of receiving the record and the draft plan, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard).
  • Service Manager: copy each answer marked REG-SBS-01 to the practice sheet row within 2 business days of each entry (our standard).
  • Practitioner: update question 33 on the day the authorisation status changes.
  • Practitioner: lodge the plan and answer question 31 within 5 business days of the plan being finalised (our standard). The Service Manager prepares the lodgement and keeps the date and reference.
  • Practitioner: add an entry at question 35 after each progress check. Checks are at least every 3 months while the practice is in the plan.
  • File the record on the participant's file with the plan, in a restricted folder.
  • Keep it for 7 years from the day of the last entry (our standard). The law of [state or territory] can require longer.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of every behaviour support plan [Provider name] writes. It has three sheets. On the plan sheet each row is one plan version. It shows when we were engaged and who wrote the plan. It shows what the agreed to and which accepted the plan. It shows whether the plan reached the Commissioner on time and when it is next due for review. On the practice sheet each row is one in one plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, and holds the answers FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record routes here, with every authorisation status the practice has held. On the incident review sheet each row is one review under FRM-SBS-06 Restrictive Practice Incident Review Record of an emergency or unauthorised use, keyed on the plan number in col A.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 40 (1) to s 40 (6). The register also holds the plan dates and records that s 39, s 41, s 42, s 43 and s 44 rely on. Those threads write to the columns marked with their indicators.
  • Legal basis: the Behaviour Support Rules. Sections 17 and 18 say who writes. Section 19 sets time limits. Section 20 says how plans are developed and section 21 what they contain. Sections 22 to 24 cover review, form and lodgement.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day the plan is superseded or ends (our standard). We set it to match the 7 years in section 15(3) of the Behaviour Support Rules for records of the use of a regulated restrictive practice.
  • Other law can require longer, for example for records about a child. For a participant under 18, keep the row until they turn 25 or for 7 years, whichever is later (our standard pending state law). Check REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register and the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Columns H and I are worked out and never typed over. Columns AB, AC, AD and AW are filled only when col Z lists a regulated restrictive practice, and summarise the practice sheet. Columns AN to AP are filled only when col AM is yes. Columns AR to BA are filled from the forms named in the Filled from column. The practice sheet columns RP-A to RP-R are filled from FRM-SBS-02, one row per practice per plan. The incident review sheet columns IR-A to IR-O are filled from FRM-SBS-06, one row per review; col AZ summarises them.
register.entry:
1. The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole does both. Open the row on the day we confirm the referral (our standard).
  2. Use one row for each plan version. A new version is a new row. Link it to the one it replaces in col D and col BD.
  3. The Practitioner gives each answer to the Service Manager within 1 of recording it on the form. The forms are FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record for the plan sheet, and FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record for the practice sheet. The Service Manager enters it within 2 business days of the stage (our standard).
  4. Columns that hold a list (col R, col Z, col AC, col AD, col AG, col AK, col AW and col BB, and practice sheet cols RP-P and RP-R) take a new dated line for each change. Never overwrite a line. An authorisation status is never typed over: every status the practice has held stays visible with its date.
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Never type over a worked-out date. To change the engagement date in col F, record the reason and the name of the who agreed.
  7. When systems are down, use the paper forms. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back.
  8. When a row is about the work of the Service Manager or the Practitioner who keeps it, the Chief Executive holds it. When it is about the Chief Executive, the Clinical Supervisor holds it. In a sole practitioner provider the Practitioner keeps every row, and the outside Clinical Supervisor reviews them every month under How we review.
  9. The practice sheet is the second sheet of this register: one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, with cols RP-A to RP-R. Open a practice row when col Z first lists or proposes the practice. The incident review sheet is the third sheet: one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, keyed on col A, with cols IR-A to IR-O; open a row when a review starts and summarise it in col AZ. A small provider can keep the other list columns on a further sheet in the same way; each line carries the plan number from col A.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the plan has been replaced by a later version that is in force, or the plan has ended, or the participant has left us, and col BD says which
  • every lodgement is done and recorded in col AO
  • every open line in col BB is done, or has moved to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the Service Manager has checked the row and recorded the closing date.
